messages:
Maria D: Quick check-in — I'm iterating on the 'heap lease' idea for cross-device ownership. sketch: a borrower gets a short-lived lease token that pins residency and gives a single-writer handle. Returning a lease either returns ownership or converts to a shared-read marker. Thoughts?

Ashwin R: sounds promising. two quick concerns: 1) how do we enforce single-writer across CPU/GPU without heavy fences? 2) what about fragmentation when lots of short leases churn?

Taylor L: For (1) we can use an epoch counter + lightweight fencing at handoff. borrower increments epoch; owner waits until epoch >= value. avoids full GPU sync for common-case read.

Kevin M: For (2) we should differentiate short-lived vs long-lived allocations at allocation time. short-live => pooled slab with compaction off; long-live => pinned arenas. prevents small leases from scattering hot pages.

Sasha P: API ergonomics: prefer explicit "acquireLease(handle, mode) -> leaseToken" and `leaseToken.release(returnPolicy)` where returnPolicy in {KeepPinned, DropToShared, ReturnOwnership}. Keep semantics obvious to integrators.

Maria D: fwiw I'm leaning to three return states. KeepPinned (fast path), DropToShared (make it read-only and allow coalesce), ReturnOwnership (handoff to next owner).

Ashwin R: Implementation detail: make lease tokens opaque 64-bit values with embedded flags + a short-circuit field for "no-ops" when lease is no longer needed (helps remote callers).

Taylor L: Concern: race on ReturnOwnership — if a slow consumer holds a stale token we could double-allocate. We should attach an incarnation id + sequence number and verify on return. If mismatch, return is a NOP and we schedule reclaim.

Kevin M: Eviction interplay: leases must be respected by eviction. Evictor should consult live-lease bitmap first. We can keep a bloom filter per arena for mem-efficient checks (false positives OK -> conservative eviction).

Sasha P: Telemetry/rollout: expose counters for lease_handoffs, lease_misses, lease_stale_returns. Add an enforced canary where short-lived leases are used by a single model for 48h before wider rollout.

Maria D: Perf targets — keep common path (acquire -> read -> release KeepPinned) < 1.5us end-to-end on our 8xA100 host. If epochs add 200-300ns it's ok.

runtime-bot: deploy-prod notice: rolling canary group "lease-proto" created, 3 nodes tagged.

Ashwin R: API sketch (pseudo):
```
// C++ style
LeaseToken t = heap.acquireLease(obj, LeaseMode::Write);
// do GPU work (no full fence)
heap.releaseLease(t, ReturnPolicy::ReturnOwnership);
```
Make sure the release path can be called from either CPU or GPU thread safely.

Taylor L: For GPU->CPU handoff we need a small wait-on-fence inside releaseLease when ReturnOwnership requested. But default KeepPinned should skip waits.

Kevin M: Data layout note: store lease metadata in a small header per page (8B) so scanning for live leases is cheap. Avoid per-allocation locks.

Sasha P: Security/bugs: add asserts in dev builds that try to re-acquire a write lease while one exists. Also add an escape hatch env var to disable leasing for problematic models.

Maria D: rollout plan: 1) implement token + epoch + header; 2) unit tests for concurrent handoff; 3) local perf microbench; 4) canary on non-critical models; 5) collect telemetry for 2 weeks and iterate.

Ashwin R: I'll prototype epoch checks + NOP-on-stale-return tomorrow morning.

Taylor L: I'll take slab/pool policy hooks — need an API from allocator to mark hot vs churny.

Kevin M: I'll wire eviction bloom filter prototype.

Sasha P: I'll prepare the telemetry dashboard and alert thresholds (lease_miss_rate > 0.5% -> pager).

Maria D: Awesome. If anything else crops up, drop it here. Also: try to pick names other than "lease" if we end up shipping (branding). :thinking_face:
